page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384-metal is a bare-metal server instance architected on the x86_64 instruction set. It provides 384 dedicated vCPUs accompanied by 768.0 GB of physical RAM, producing a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures complete hardware isolation and unshared processing capacity across all 384 execution threads.

The hardware configuration features zero local NVMe or bundled disk storage, making persistent operations reliant on remote network storage volumes. Furthermore, the platform contains no GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon deployment. The omission of attached storage and specialized graphical hardware targets workloads strictly focused on raw host processing.

From an efficiency standpoint, the high core count provides high compute density for parallel tasks while keeping memory resource costs aligned with workloads that do not require extensive RAM buffers. The core tradeoff is the fixed 2.0 GB per-core boundary, which limits utility for memory-heavy databases or large in-memory caches. Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384-metal is primarily suited for compute-intensive workloads such as distributed batch processing, parallel compilation pipelines, code builds, and high-concurrency scientific modeling.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384-metal is a bare-metal compute-focused instance powered by x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 768.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a compute-optimized allocation of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes zero integrated GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be serviced externally. The architecture is designed to maximize thread concurrency across a large core count, offering favorable hardware density and operational cost efficiency for CPU-bound applications that do not demand extensive per-core memory overhead. Tradeoffs involve relying completely on network block storage and navigating memory bounds on tasks exceeding 2.0 GB per execution thread. It is particularly suited for high-density compute workloads, massive batch processing, video encoding, continuous integration pipelines, and compute-heavy mathematical or scientific modeling.
